Slovakia’s Retail and Services Sectors Hit by Nationwide Norovirus Outbreak

Slovakia’s economy is facing mounting pressure as a nationwide norovirus outbreak continues to disrupt daily life, with strict health measures in place for the second consecutive week. The government ordered the closure of schools, indoor dining, cinemas, and gyms last Monday in an effort to contain the highly contagious virus, which has been confirmed in all eight regions.

Retail and hospitality sectors have reported steep declines, with the Slovak Retail Association estimating foot traffic in major shopping districts has dropped by over 60% compared to the same period last year. “We urge the government to provide emergency support for small businesses, which are facing unsustainable losses,” said Zuzana Krajcikova, the association’s president.

Public transport remains operational with reduced capacity, while factories and logistics hubs have been encouraged to maintain strict hygiene protocols but are not subject to closure. The Ministry of Finance forecasts a potential 0.7% contraction in GDP for the quarter if restrictions persist through month-end. “Our priority is public health, but we recognize the economic challenges,” Finance Minister Miroslav Hlinka said at a press conference Tuesday.

Unemployment claims have ticked up, with the National Labor Union reporting nearly 9,000 new applications since the closures began. Analysts at Central Europe Economic Insight predict the service sector will bear the brunt, with lasting effects possible if the measures extend into March.

The government is expected to review the restrictions next week, but health officials warn that reopening too soon could risk a resurgence. Testing and contact tracing efforts have been ramped up nationwide.
